I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stay with the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits my weather, my water situation, my machinery, and the way I know how to work. At the start of the growing season, my main job is to carry the winter wheat through jointing, heading, and grain filling, then bring in summer maize right after wheat harvest so I do not lose heat or moisture. I will use improved or hybrid seed rather than traditional seed because I care about stable yield and better stress tolerance more than saving on seed. For wheat, I will put more focus on nitrogen and a steady water supply, because that is what usually decides whether I get a full head and good grain weight. For maize, I will push planting quickly after wheat, keep fertilizer balanced, and control weeds and insects on time, because late sowing costs me yield fast here. I will use rotary tillage for wheat establishment after maize, and mostly no-tillage or very light disturbance for maize after wheat harvest to save time and hold soil moisture. I am choosing a straightforward wheat-maize rotation because it is the most practical system for me, it matches local conditions, and it gives me the best chance of stable income with work I know I can manage well.
